name: Nick Rallis

views.text: Fit the defense to the players you have instead of forcing them into a rigid system.
Energy and emotion are different things; a staff needs the energy and a clear, calm head.
Age is neither an edge nor a handicap for a coach; what matters is how much you keep learning.
Play every snap with the relentless effort of your best competitor, and make the rest match it.
Pressure can be manufactured with scheme when you do not have elite rushers.
Focus on the day in front of you; the timetable takes care of itself.

signatures: separates staying calm from being quiet when he describes his own style
holds up one veteran as the model for how the whole defense should play
want: to prove the league's youngest coordinator can out-think older play-callers with less talent
fear: that his youth becomes the explanation whenever the defense falls short
voice: Steady, earnest and precise for a young coach; he talks about problem-solving and keeping a clear head more than about himself. He credits Gannon and his best players and avoids grand claims. His voice is upbeat but controlled.

evidence.summary: Gannon picks Rallis, 29, his Eagles linebackers coach who started under him in Minnesota in 2018; Rallis says he cares less about limited experience than about accumulating as much knowledge as he can. Team site.
Report of the hire: two seasons as Eagles linebackers coach with Gannon after three with the Vikings, from quality control in 2018 to assistant linebackers coach in 2020. Background only.

At his introduction he calls himself high-energy but separates energy from emotion, stresses a calm, consistent mind for solving problems, names Budda Baker as the model, and wants an aggressive defense; Gannon says he trusts him fully. Team site.

He says he came largely because of Gannon, whom he trusts personally and professionally, points to Baker's relentless effort as the standard, and argues a staff needs both composure and energy. Local outlet.

He describes an adaptable defense built around available players, wants physical high-energy play, sees no edge or handicap in his age, and jokes with Gannon over a borrowed catchphrase; singles out Baker. Student newsroom report.

Names Rallis the team's 2024 coach of the year for lifting a thin defense from near the bottom to 15th in scoring and far better against the run, crediting creative pressure schemes. A writer's assessment.
